summary: chai-as-buffered exfiltrates process.env and executes remote JavaScript on require
details: On require of the package, lib/initializeCaller.js POSTs the full contents of process.env via axios to a hardcoded base64-obfuscated endpoint that decodes to https://ipcheck-hashed.vercel.app/api/auth/13b72bec1d4f2ee1c661, then passes the response body to new Function('require', response.data) and invokes it with the module's require, giving the remote server arbitrary code execution in the Node process of any installer that loads the package. The package.json metadata and exported no-op middleware present a logger/middleware cover story unrelated to the actual payload, and the destination URL is base64-encoded to evade review. The name also resembles the legitimate chai-as-promised assertion helper, consistent with a typosquat lure.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
